newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks climb higher on Clinton, rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks climb higher on Clinton, rate cut.

text.p: Norwegian stocks continued an upward path on Wednesday in line with general bullish sentiment due to U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election and the surprise day-earlier rate cut by Norway's central bank.
Trade was robust with turnover topping more than one billion crowns. Dealers said they expected the finance and consumer sectors to remain buoyant in wake of the reduction in interest rates.
Oslo's Total share index gained 0.3 percent to close at 881.13 point, off the day's high at 883.42 points.
All sectors traded in positive territory with the exception of insurance which suffered from a decline in Norway's largest insurer Storebrand.
Dealers said Storebrand came under selling pressure due to limited upside potential on the share dprice and after slightly weaker-than-expected nine month results.
The stock fell 1.50 crowns, or almost four percent, to end at 36.90 crowns.
Kvaerner continued to build on recent gains on rumours of possible contract awards. Kvaerner A closed 5.50 crowns up at 256 crowns.
